text:
maya: deploy-bot kicked off staged rollout -> service=generator, version=v3.2.1, target=5% across us-west-2/eu-west-1, change-window=overnight UTC
deploy-bot: [automated] rollout started: id=rl-20260318-01, 5% traffic -> v3.2.1. Monitoring enabled.
aj: quick heads up — 95p latency for /generate is up from 180ms -> ~420ms in us-west-2, started ~3m after rollout.
sanjay: linking logs — https://logs.redwood.internal/r/rl-20260318-01?filter=us-west-2 — showing a pattern of redispatches and kvcache misses.
linh: can we confirm this is only on the redispatch path? any error spikes?
emily: no increase in 500s, just tail latency and a handful of higher token-generation durations.
aj: snippet from trace (ops-bot pasted):
```
TraceID: abc123
step: token_dispatch
reason: redispatch_to_cold_shard
duration_ms: 320
kv_cache_hit: false
```

maya: that pattern looks like the new model variant changed kv keys; cache miss -> redispatch -> tail spike. Not necessarily correctness issue but impacts SLA.
ops-bot: metric alert: generator.95p.latency(us-west-2) above threshold (300ms) for 2m.
sanjay: recommend hold at 5% and pin traffic to v3.2.0 while we investigate. Can we do a quick rollback?
maya: agree. Change window still open for a few hours but we should be conservative. Anyone object to holding and pinning?
linh: +1. also suggest adding a small routing rule to avoid sending long-context requests to v3.2.1 until we validate kv layout.
emily: can we patch runtime to bypass redispatcher as a mitigation (cheap short-term)?
aj: that might reduce throughput. Quickest is pin/rollback. We can test a config change in staging for the bypass.
deploy-bot: [action] initiating hold: rollout id=rl-20260318-01 -> hold at 5%. Rolling back new route for key=producer:generator. Traffic pinned to v3.2.0 for all regions.
maya: noted. Sanjay, can you start a short postmortem checklist: collect traces, confirm kv key hash differences, run small repro with sample prompts?
sanjay: on it. I'll capture a reproducible request set and run against v3.2.0/v3.2.1 and share diffs.
linh: ops: once pinned, can we run a canary on a dedicated pool with traffic=1% and special debug flags so we can gather more detailed traces without impacting customers?
ops-bot: scheduled ephemeral debug pool: id=dbg-rl-20260318-01, target=1%, regions=us-west-2, retention=6h.
emily: also add release notes entry: "v3.2.1 introduces kv-key normalization; investigating redispatch latency in some shards." keep wording neutral.
maya: agree. Emily, please push that to release notes and include rollback decision and mitigation steps.
emily: done: https://docs.redwood.internal/releases/v3.2.1-notes (draft) — added mitigation + contact list.
aj: timeline proposal: hold + pin now, collect traces for 30-60m, if no fix or clear root cause, rollback fully and schedule a smaller targeted rollout after fixes. Does that work?
linh: yep. Also flag adjacent services for possible cache churn.
sanjay: collecting traces now, will post repro within 20m.
maya: thanks. decision: HOLD (pin to v3.2.0) — no further traffic increases. Ops to monitor 95p and error rates. If metric returns to baseline and root cause identified -> resume canary with debug pool. Otherwise prepare full rollback in 45m.
aj: :thumbsup:
deploy-bot: [note] rollout rl-20260318-01 status=held, pinned_version=v3.2.0, debug_pool=dbg-rl-20260318-01
ops-bot: monitoring alert suppressed for current incident; continuing capture.
linh: leaving a quick checklist here: 1) collect traces (sanjay) 2) compare kv-key hashes (runtime team) 3) test redispatch bypass in staging (aj) 4) draft rollback playbook (maya)
sanjay: uploaded trace bundle: https://artifacts.redwood.internal/trace-bundles/rl-20260318-01.zip
emily: uploaded release note draft + rollback rationale to the release tracker.
maya: thank you all — keep updates in this thread. If anybody sees other region impact, ping on-call immediately.
aj: will post an update in 20m with staging bypass test results.
linh: +1 on that cadence.
emily: adding a short customer-facing blurb we can reuse if rollback goes full: "We observed elevated tail latency for a small percentage of requests during a staged rollout and paused the rollout to investigate. Customers on affected regions have been routed back to the prior version while we fix the issue."
maya: good. closing note: HOLD maintained. Next decision checkpoint at +45m or earlier if significant change.
